key_idea: The drill is axis-parallel, so project the points onto the three coordinate planes and take the smallest of the three minimum enclosing circles.
sketch: Run Welzl's randomized incremental minimum enclosing circle (expected O(n)) on the xy, yz and zx projections and print twice the smallest radius. Uses long double, a small containment epsilon, and a fallback to the widest pair for (near-)collinear triples. Pitfalls: shuffling is mandatory for the expected linear time (n=5000 makes the O(n^3) worst case too slow), and output is the diameter, not the radius.
